title: PCR enters the batch score with the wrong sign
what: Raw scib.me.pcr (batch variance LEFT; higher = worse) is added with +1 instead of scIB's pcr_comparison=(pre-post)/pre.
evidence: Re-verified: scib 1.1.7 source; stored pcr is highest for unintegrated (0.189) and lowest for scVI (0.014).
affects: Every batch & scIB number, ranks, frontier tables. Re-scoring is cheap (post-hoc from stored columns; no refits).

title: Models trained on log-normalized values stored as 'counts'
what: Prep copies the source X (already log-normalized) into layers['counts']; the true integer counts in the source are discarded. All scVI-family arms and scvi/scanvi baselines fit an NB/ZINB likelihood to non-count data; PCA/harmony/scanorama see double-normalized X.
evidence: Re-verified on immune/lung/atac_small: prepped counts 100% non-integer (max <10); source layers['counts'] integer (max 2654/256/51). Pancreas source counts are themselves partly non-integer.
affects: All 6,305 latents. Direction of effect on headline comparisons unknown; one 30-epoch test changed disc mixing 0.82->0.50 (provisional). Requires re-prep + re-fit.

title: Critic > discriminator headline depends on the summary statistic
what: Headline averages over a shared nominal λ grid; arms' loss scales differ, so this measures robustness-to-λ, not attainable performance. At cross-validated λ the stored scores favour the discriminator.
evidence: My recompute (leave-one-seed-out λ selection): stored scIB -> critics beat disc 4-5/16 cells; with C1 fixed -> reference 11/16 (p=0.04), pooled 9/16, barycenter 8/16, 3-critic mean +0.012 (p=0.18).

title: 'scVI' baseline is a different model than the arms' base
what: All 6,160 adversarial configs and the λ=0 control are UNCONDITIONED (adversary is the sole integrator), 239 ep, bs 512, no early stopping. scVI baseline is batch-CONDITIONED, ≤200 ep, early stopping, bs 128.
evidence: Re-verified: cond=0 in 2000+4160 manifest rows; baseline code reads setup_anndata(batch_key=...), max_epochs=200, early_stopping=True. scVI − none(nl) ≈ +0.057 scIB before any adversary.
affects: Every 'adversary vs scVI' claim, incl. today's difficulty-stratified figure.

title: Sinkhorn gradient driven by a detached scale -> latent contraction
what: Normalising z by a no_grad scale makes shrinking all of z an easy way to lower the loss; recomputed each step, so the encoder keeps contracting.
evidence: Re-verified code; sampled latents: median max|z| sinkhorn 2.3, barycenter 0.7 vs none 5.4. Training agent: cos(grad,z)=0.6-0.8; attached-scale variant changes mixing (1 dataset, 80 ep, provisional).
affects: All sinkhorn results ('Sinkhorn weakest'); MMD less so (high λ).

title: Reference critic aligns to the alphabetically-first batch
what: Index-0 batch is often a small batch (atac_large: 4.3% of cells); the project's entropy rule is not used on the final path.
evidence: Differs from entropy rule on 6/8 datasets.

title: Critics (esp. barycenter) and Sinkhorn lower their loss by shrinking the latent
what: W1 and fixed-eps Sinkhorn are not scale-invariant; scIB metrics are, so collapsed latents still score.
evidence: max|z|<1 in 78-100% of barycenter configs at λ≥50; 33/80 sinkhorn configs collapsed at prereg λ=200.

title: Robustness attribution overclaims ('property of the JS objective')
what: Discriminator generator loss is unbounded max-CE (not scvi's bounded fool loss), disc_iter=1 vs 10 + GP for critics, no clipping.
evidence: Code reading; inflation of disc latents on the failing datasets; causal link not shown.
affects: Wording of the 'every divergence is the discriminator' claim.
